rows.evidence: Q1: Application section and Results <U+2013> the authors run MOBIDIC-WRM daily over the Arno basin for 1992<U+2013>2006 at 200 m cells, calibrate on 15 sub-basins and compare modelled with measured flow duration curves (Fig. 2) and daily discharge (Fig. 3). Q2: Application section states land cover, geology and soil hydraulic properties were retrieved from existing maps and remote-sensing data; Water budget section and Fig. 5/Table 2 <U+2013> water budget WB = Q <U+2212> EF <U+2212> W computed for 44 sections, sub-basins classified by number of summer days below environmental flow and mapped as extreme/severe/moderate/null, with the text stating that each critical level corresponds to different government requirements such as constraints on new withdrawal permissions, and that results formed the basis of the Water Budget Management Plan. Q4: Eq. 13<U+2013>14 and Fig. 2<U+2013>3 <U+2013> the intermediate variable (modelled natural discharge net of withdrawals versus the Q7,2 environmental flow, i.e. residual flow and days below EF) is explicitly modelled and the discharge component is checked against gauged flow duration curves. Q6: Application and Water budget sections <U+2013> effect reported for the whole ~8000 km2 Arno basin, 15 sub-basins and 44 river sections (Fig. 5). Q8: Results <U+2013> poor agreement at stations where groundwater dynamics need more detailed representation than the lumped approach; Groundwater section and Application <U+2013> simplified linear-reservoir groundwater scheme used because aquifer data are scarce; Fig. 3 discussion <U+2013> peaks and low base flows estimated with varying accuracy.
rows.notes: Remote sensing plays only a supporting role here: it supplies some input layers (land cover, soil properties) to a distributed hydrological model; the application's calibration/validation used river gauges, not the remotely-sensed land-surface-temperature maps mentioned in the abstract. The identification of critical sub-areas and the link to withdrawal restrictions rest on the model's water budget, and the criticality map itself is not validated against observed deficits. Q2 is answered yes because the review's 'tools' are the EO-fed model and the discharge output is compared with measurements, but the attribution to remote sensing per se is weak. Sub-basins within one basin are not treated as distinct regions for Q5. No dispersion or uncertainty propagation is reported for the deficit classification (Q9 no). Data-requirement remarks concern the detailed groundwater option, not the claimed effect, so Q7 no.
